# pEigen

> pEigen is a Python package that exposes Eigen's dense and sparse linear algebra through a NumPy/SciPy-native API. It is installed with `pip install peigentux` (or `pip install "peigentux[sparse]"` for the SciPy-based sparse routines) and imported as `peigen`. Its main feature is a reusable sparse Cholesky / LDLᵀ factorization that needs no SuiteSparse. MIT licensed; bundles Eigen under MPL-2.0.

Key facts:

- The distribution name is `peigentux`, but the import name is `peigen`. `pip install peigen` installs an unrelated project.
- Current version: 2.1.0. Wheels for CPython 3.10–3.15 on Linux (x86_64, aarch64; OpenBLAS) and macOS (arm64, x86_64; Accelerate). No Windows, musllinux or free-threaded wheels.
- All routines work in real float64. Integer and float32 input is converted; complex input raises TypeError.
- Sparse input may be any SciPy sparse format (`*_matrix` or `*_array`); it is never modified in place. Dimensions and nonzero counts must fit in 32-bit indices.
- Modules: `peigen.linalg` (dense), `peigen.sparse` (sparse; needs SciPy), `peigen.decomp` (reusable decomposition objects). `peigen.show_build_config()` reports the linked BLAS/LAPACK.

## Docs

- [Install](https://peigentux.com/install.html): pip commands, supported platforms, building from source, checking the BLAS/LAPACK backend
- [Algorithms](https://peigentux.com/algorithms.html): every function with its Eigen class or LAPACK routine, a "which solver should I use" table, and error conventions
- [Examples](https://peigentux.com/examples.html): complete runnable programs (Poisson solve, time stepping with refactorize, GMRF log-likelihood and sampling, KKT systems, sparse LU, CG, dense least squares, PCA)
- [Benchmarks](https://peigentux.com/benchmarks.html): timings against NumPy, SciPy SuperLU and CHOLMOD, including where pEigen is slower

## API summary

- `peigen.linalg.matmul(a, b)`; `solve(a, b, *, method="auto"|"lapack"|"eigen")` (LAPACK dgesv or Eigen PartialPivLU); `qr(a, *, mode="reduced"|"complete")` (Householder QR); `svd(a, *, full_matrices=False, method="auto"|"lapack"|"bdcsvd")` (dgesdd or Eigen BDCSVD); `eigh(a, *, lower=True, eigenvectors=True, method="auto"|"lapack"|"eigen")` and `eighvals(a, ...)` (dsyevd or SelfAdjointEigenSolver); `norm(a, ord=None, axis=None, keepdims=False)`.
- `peigen.sparse.cholesky(a, *, mode="ldlt"|"llt"|"multifrontal", ordering="amd"|"natural", lower=True, shift=0.0)` returns `SparseCholesky` with `solve(b)`, `refactorize(a, *, shift=None)` (same sparsity pattern, numeric phase only), `slogdet()`, `logdet()`, `inertia` (positive, negative, zero eigenvalue counts), `L()`, `D()`, `P()` (factors as SciPy CSC and the permutation index array `p`, with `(A + shift*I)[p][:, p] == L @ D @ L.T`; `L` has its diagonal stored, unit except for llt; `D` has 2x2 blocks for multifrontal and is the identity for llt; sample x ~ N(0, As^{-1}) by solving `L.T y = D^{-1/2} z` and setting `x[p] = y`), `factor_nnz`, `shift`, `mode`, `ordering`, `shape`. It factors `P (A + shift*I) P^T`, reads one triangle, raises `numpy.linalg.LinAlgError` on breakdown, and releases the GIL in `solve`.
  - `mode="ldlt"` (default): Eigen SimplicialLDLT, for SPD matrices with low fill.
  - `mode="llt"`: SimplicialLLT; fails unless positive definite.
  - `mode="multifrontal"` (experimental): Eigen MultifrontalLDLT, with 1x1/2x2 threshold pivoting. Use it for symmetric indefinite (KKT/saddle-point) matrices and high-fill problems such as 3D meshes.
- `peigen.sparse.factorize(a)` returns `SparseFactorized` (Eigen SparseLU) with `solve(b)`, for general square matrices.
- `peigen.sparse.solve(a, b, *, method="auto"|"lu"|"cholesky"|"cg"|"bicgstab", tol=1e-8, maxiter=None, preconditioner="none"|"jacobi"|"ichol"|"ilu", ilu_fill_factor=10, ilu_drop_tol=1e-4)`. `"ichol"` is zero-fill incomplete Cholesky (Eigen IncompleteCholesky); `"ilu"` with CG is deprecated. Iterative methods raise RuntimeError if they do not converge, judged by the true residual. `solve_stats(a, b, method="cg", ...)` returns `{"iterations", "error", "residual"}` (`error` is Eigen's estimate, `residual` the true ‖b − Ax‖/‖b‖).
- `peigen.sparse.spmm(a, b)` (sparse @ dense), `spspmm(a, b)` (sparse @ sparse, returns CSC), `to_dense(a)`, `from_coo(data, row, col, shape)`.
- `peigen.decomp.SVD(a, full_matrices=False).solve(b, rcond=None)` (minimum-norm least squares; rcond relative to max singular value); `peigen.decomp.QR(a, mode="reduced").solve(b)` (square or tall, full column rank); `decomp.SparseFactorized`, `decomp.SparseCholesky` (aliases of the sparse classes).

## Usage notes

- Prefer `sparse.cholesky` over `sparse.solve(..., method="lu")` for symmetric positive definite matrices; keep the factorization object to solve with more right-hand sides later.
- A 2D right-hand side `b` of shape (n, k) is solved in one blocked pass; that is much faster than looping over columns.
- For symmetric indefinite matrices use `mode="multifrontal"`; `mode="ldlt"` does not pivot for stability.
- For CG use `preconditioner="ichol"` (symmetric incomplete Cholesky). `preconditioner="ilu"` with CG is deprecated (DeprecationWarning, removal in 3.0): IncompleteLUT is not symmetric and fails to converge on a 2D Laplacian at the default `ilu_fill_factor=10`.
- `tol` for `method="cg"`/`"bicgstab"` is checked against the true relative residual ‖b − Ax‖/‖b‖ after the solve, not only Eigen's recursive estimate (which BiCGSTAB can drift away from). If the true residual is more than 10x above `tol`, the solver restarts from its current iterate (up to 5 times, within `maxiter`) and raises RuntimeError if it still misses, so a returned solution meets `tol` within that factor, and an unreachable `tol` raises.
